essence: Separate planting sheets help Iona Reed recover garden details that would otherwise be forgotten by the following season.
brief: Reed keeps a sheet for each garden bed, marking dates, layout and small surprises. Finding an old sheet brought back a delayed planting, and a torn corner recalled beans washed away by rain. The records explain gaps in a harvest while leaving open what a different spring might have brought.
understanding: For four seasons Reed has sketched each bed separately. An overlooked sheet recovered the timing of a late planting that the main notebook did not bring to mind.
A simple plan can preserve both deliberate choices and accidents. On one sheet a torn corner recorded where rain removed a row of beans.
Reed values the record for what it can recover months later. Knowing that rain removed beans gives context for a poor harvest, but offers no comparison with a drier year.
